tema: Modals of Deduction — Present (Must Be, Can't Be, Must Be Doing)

cast_dialogue.linea: Present deductions with continuous forms, heroes: not just what IS true, but what is HAPPENING right now.
Listen — someone's playing the piano upstairs. It must be the new neighbour.
It can't be Mr. Lopez — he moved out last week. And it can't be a recording: the tempo keeps changing.
Whoever it is, they must be practising for hours every day. It sounds beautiful!
Someone is knocking at my door at this hour... It must be Ben — he can't be working so late again!

banco_oraciones.oracion: It must be the new neighbour.
Someone must be practising every day.
It can't be Mr. Lopez — he moved out.
It can't be a recording — the tempo changes.
He can't be sleeping — the lights are on.
Who can that be at the door?
What must they be doing upstairs?
Is that the neighbour? It must be.
Is he at the gym? He can't be — he's at work.
Is she practising? She might be.

banner_diagnostico.opcion_a: Someone must be practise the piano upstairs.
banner_diagnostico.opcion_b: Someone must be practising the piano upstairs.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Present deductions: must be + noun/adjective (states) and must be + verb-ing (actions happening now). The same for can't and might. Continuous form for actions in progress: 'He must be working', 'She can't be sleeping'.

ejercicios.pregunta: It ___ Mr. Lopez — he moved out last week.
The tempo keeps changing, so it ___ a recording.

ejercicios.afirmacion: For actions happening now we use 'must be + verb-ing'.
'He must be work late' is correct.

ejercicios.texto: They must be ___ (practise) for hours every day.
He can't be ___ (sleep) — the lights are on.

ejercicios.texto_con_error: Someone must be practise the piano upstairs.
ejercicios.respuesta: Someone must be practising the piano upstairs.

ejercicios.oracion_base: I'm sure she is working late.

ejercicios.pregunta: Deduce three things about your neighbours right now (must be, can't be, might be + -ing).
ejercicios.respuesta: The neighbours must be cooking — it smells great. They can't be sleeping — the TV is loud. They might be having a party.

guion: Ben: Listen — someone's playing the piano in the flat upstairs.
Sofía: It must be the new neighbour. She plays beautifully.
Ben: Are you sure? It could be Mr. Lopez.
Sofía: It can't be him — he moved out last week.
Kenji: And it can't be a recording. The tempo keeps changing.
Sofía: Whoever it is, they must be practising for hours every day.
Ben: Well, they can't be practising now — the music just stopped.

comprension.pregunta: Who does Sofía think is playing?
Why can't it be a recording?

reading.texto: Listen — someone is playing the piano in the flat upstairs. It can't be Mr. Lopez, because he moved out last week. It must be the new neighbour; Sofía says she plays beautifully. It can't be a recording, because the tempo keeps changing. Whoever it is, they must be practising for hours every day. Ben can't be hearing it, though — he is at work and his flat is two streets away.

preguntas.afirmacion: The tempo of the music changes.
Ben lives in the flat upstairs.

partes.parte: A — Completa con must be, can't be o might be (+ -ing si hay acción)

ejercicios.texto: Listen! Someone ___ playing the piano upstairs. (certainty)
It ___ Mr. Lopez — he moved out last week. (impossible)
They ___ practising for hours every day. (certainty, action)
He ___ working late, but I'm not sure. (possibility)

partes.parte: B — Reescribe con must be / can't be

ejercicios.texto: I'm sure she is working late. →
I'm sure they are having a party. →
Corrige: 'Someone must be practise the piano.'
Corrige: 'He can't to be sleeping — the lights are on.'
Escribe 3 deducciones sobre lo que está pasando ahora cerca de ti (must/can't/might be + -ing).

answer_key: 7. They must be having a party.
8. Someone must be practising the piano.
9. He can't be sleeping — the lights are on.
10. Respuesta libre (ej. 'My neighbour must be cooking. The dog can't be sleeping — it's barking. Someone might be watching TV.')
